title: Empowering knowledge graphs with hybrid retrieval-augmented generation for the intelligent mix scheme of mass concrete
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about an intelligent concrete mix design system for hydraulic engineering; the vector database is used only as a retrieval component within a RAG pipeline and is not the subject of analysis, improvement, benchmarking, or survey.
research_focus: Proposing an intelligent dam concrete mix proportioning system (DCMPS) based on a RAG framework that integrates a domain-specific knowledge graph with vector-based semantic retrieval and LLM-driven reasoning to generate mix design schemes targeting strength, durability, and crack resistance.
method: A knowledge graph was constructed from 1723 mix proportioning records using Neo4j, encoded with the M3E embedding model into a vector database for cosine-similarity-based retrieval, and combined with a hierarchical prompt-engineering reasoning architecture where an LLM performs comparative analysis on retrieved cases to generate tailored mix designs.
indexing_methods: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor, mentioned as future work); cosine similarity
application_domain: Dam concrete mix proportioning in hydraulic and hydroelectric engineering
results_summary: The DCMPS was validated on a test dataset and demonstrated superior overall performance compared to a larger-parameter native LLM, achieving higher reasoning adequacy and accuracy. Case studies confirmed that the recommended mix designs closely aligned with target performance requirements for strength, durability, and crack resistance. The knowledge augmentation approach significantly enhanced the performance of smaller models, confirming the value of external knowledge retrieval. The system also improved interpretability by enabling comparison of relevant cases and analysis of material influence mechanisms alongside the generated designs.
limitations: Newly added data require manual review to ensure accuracy of entity matching; As the KG node scale expands to hundreds of thousands, the existing retrieval mechanism faces linearly increasing response times
research_gaps: Collecting and incorporating a broader range of mix proportion data into the KG to enhance comprehensiveness; Developing a DCMP performance prediction system capable of forecasting performance parameters from predefined mix compositions; Deploying the system in real-world engineering projects to collect on-site feedback for continuous training and self-evolution; Introducing a distributed Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexing framework to optimize retrieval at scale; Developing automated entity alignment tools to enhance efficiency of data ingestion

title: Intelligent Q&A System for Welding Processes Based on a Symmetric KG-DB Hybrid-RAG Strategy
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is a Hybrid-RAG Q&A system for ship welding; the vector database is used as one of two retrieval components but is not analyzed, benchmarked, or improved as a technology in its own right.
research_focus: Addressing the limitations of traditional RAG (high retrieval noise, low accuracy for complex procedural queries) in the ship welding domain by proposing a symmetric Hybrid-RAG strategy that combines a knowledge graph for symbolic reasoning with a vector database for semantic retrieval.
method: A three-stage symmetric 'Generate-Retrieve-Generate' framework (SWP-Chat) using dual retrieval engines: Neo4j knowledge graph with Cypher queries for structured reasoning and a vector database for semantic retrieval, supplemented by PCA for vector dimensionality reduction and a structural-confidence fusion formula for integrating evidence from both channels.
application_domain: Ship welding process question answering and industrial decision support in manufacturing
results_summary: The proposed SWP-Chat framework achieves an F1 score of 79.35%, significantly surpassing typical RAG baselines, with a 40.89% F1 improvement over ablation variants. PCA dimensionality reduction reduces average retrieval latency by 31% while retaining over 95% of variance. Statistical testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Bonferroni correction, bootstrap resampling) confirms the improvement is statistically significant (p < 0.001, effect size r = 0.694). The symmetric generate-retrieve-generate design effectively isolates pre-retrieval noise and provides auditable, traceable answers suitable for safety-critical industrial use.
limitations: Knowledge graph maintenance relies on manual review, and incomplete KG coverage limits structured reasoning even when relevant documents exist in the vector database; Paragraph-based segmentation of the vector database can compress key procedural details into short references, causing fragments to lose critical context during retrieval; Without explicit disambiguation, identical terms may have different meanings in different process contexts, producing partial or incorrect answers
research_gaps: Automatic knowledge graph expansion and multi-source data integration with automated update mechanisms; Dynamic/adaptive chunking strategies based on syntax or topic coherence to improve semantic integrity of vector database segments; Incremental learning to improve scalability and robustness; LLM-based entity disambiguation and clarification questions to reduce query ambiguity

title: AI-DRIVEN AUTOMATION OF AIRPORT CONTRACT COMPLIANCE AND BILLING USING SAP BTP
relevance_reason: Vector databases are mentioned only once in the abstract as a component tool used for semantic clause extraction; the paper does not discuss vector database technology, indexing methods, or any core vector search research. The main subject is an AI-driven airport billing automation system.
research_focus: An AI-enhanced automation framework for airport contract compliance and billing that uses Generative AI and vector databases to semantically extract rate clauses from unstructured contracts and generate accurate invoices from real-time flight operational data.
method: A framework built on SAP Business Technology Platform combining Generative AI for semantic clause extraction, vector databases for contract clause retrieval, federated learning for cross-airport model improvement, and automated charge computation based on real-time flight data.
application_domain: Aviation airport billing, contract compliance, and financial operations
results_summary: The paper presents a prototype AI automation framework for airport billing and evaluates it on simulated enterprise datasets of 5,000 flight records across three airports. Clause extraction accuracy reached 92% compared to approximately 65% for manual extraction, representing a 41.5% improvement. End-to-end invoice generation accuracy achieved 97% alignment with reference invoices versus 85% for manual processes. Processing error rates dropped from 15% in manual workflows to 3% under automated processing, an 80% reduction. The framework also provides complete audit traceability linking billing line items to originating contract clauses.
limitations: Evaluation conducted on simulated enterprise datasets rather than real production data; Testing limited to three airports, potentially limiting generalizability; Inherent variability in aviation billing contexts spanning diverse rate structures and contractual complexity levels acknowledged as a constraint
research_gaps: Incorporation of IoT sensor data for expanded capabilities; Integration of blockchain immutability for enhanced audit trails; Multilanguage support for broader applicability across aviation service domains

title: MPC-Coder: A Dual-Knowledge Enhanced Multi-Agent System with Closed-Loop Verification for PLC Code Generation
relevance_reason: The vector database is used only as one of two knowledge sources within the MPC-Coder system for storing code snippets, and the paper does not propose, analyze, benchmark, or discuss vector database technology itself. The main subject is PLC code generation and multi-agent orchestration.
research_focus: Automated PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) code generation in industrial control, addressing the gap between ambiguous natural language requirements and the strict determinism required by control logic, through a dual-knowledge enhanced multi-agent system with closed-loop verification.
method: A dual-knowledge architecture combining a structured knowledge graph (hard constraints on process parameters) with a vector database (code snippets and function block documentation), orchestrated by five specialized agents (parsing, planning, coding, verification, fixing) in a closed-loop generation-verification-repair cycle using formal verification tools (rusty, PLCverif, nuXmv).
mentioned_systems: MPC-Coder; SWP-Chat; LLM4PLC; Vector-RAG; rusty; PLCverif; nuXmv
application_domain: Industrial control / PLC programming / thermal processing control
results_summary: The paper proposes MPC-Coder and validates it on 50 PLC code generation tasks in thermal processing control scenarios. MPC-Coder achieves 100% syntactic correctness and 78% functional consistency, significantly outperforming general-purpose LLMs (18-22% functional consistency) and a Vector-RAG baseline (56% functional consistency). Ablation experiments show that removing closed-loop verification drops syntactic correctness to 74% and functional consistency to 42%, confirming the critical role of formal verification. Convergence analysis shows the system stabilizes after 2-3 iterations, with functional failure rate decreasing from 24% to 11%. The results demonstrate that dual-knowledge fusion and closed-loop verification together effectively enhance the reliability of LLM-based industrial code generation.
limitations: Knowledge graph construction relies on domain expert involvement, requiring manual ontology design and data validation; Coverage of verification specifications is limited to predefined safety specifications, with insufficient detection of implicit constraints; Agent collaboration follows a fixed linear sequence, lacking dynamic scheduling and parallel collaboration capabilities
research_gaps: Automatic construction and evolution of knowledge graphs using LLM-based extraction and graph completion; Enhancement of verification capabilities through automatic generation of formal specifications from natural language and runtime verification; Optimization of agent collaboration with dynamic scheduling, parallel collaboration, and adversarial mutual verification; Extension to multimodal inputs such as P&ID diagrams and electrical schematics for end-to-end generation from engineering design documents

title: An elevator failure mode and effects analysis method based on retrieval augmented generation
relevance_reason: The vector database is used only as one retrieval route within a RAG pipeline for elevator FMEA; the paper does not propose, analyze, benchmark, or compare vector database systems or their indexing technology, making it a domain application that uses vector search as a tool.
research_focus: Developing an intelligent failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) method for the elevator domain using a retrieval augmented generation (RAG) framework that integrates a knowledge graph and a vector database for multi-route retrieval, combined with a novel reranking model.
method: A multi-route retrieval strategy combining keyword retrieval via a knowledge graph with similarity retrieval via a vector database, followed by a CapsGCN-Rank reranking model based on graph convolutional capsule neural networks with dynamic routing, and finally LLM-based generation of structured fault analysis results.
application_domain: Elevator maintenance and industrial fault analysis (FMEA)
results_summary: The paper proposes KG-CapsGCN-RAG, a RAG-based FMEA method for elevators that integrates a knowledge graph and a vector database in a multi-route retrieval strategy, followed by a CapsGCN-Rank reranking model. Experimental results show that KG-CapsGCN-RAG outperforms GraphRAG, LightRAG, and NaiveRAG in context precision, context recall, answer correctness, and answer relevancy. Ablation studies confirm that removing the vector database, the knowledge graph, or the reranking model each leads to measurable performance degradation. The multi-route retrieval provides broader document coverage than single-route strategies, and the CapsGCN-Rank model effectively filters redundant and low-relevance documents before LLM generation.

title: Multimodal RAG AI for Antenna Geometry Reconstruction from Scientific Literature
relevance_reason: The paper is primarily about antenna geometry reconstruction using multimodal AI and computer vision, with the vector database (Chroma/FAISS) serving only as a storage and retrieval component within a larger RAG pipeline. No in-depth analysis, comparison, or improvement of vector database technology or indexing methods is presented.
research_focus: Reconstructing antenna geometries from unstructured scientific literature (PDFs) using a Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) pipeline that combines vision-language models, vector database retrieval, OCR, and computer vision to produce CAD-ready DXF files for electromagnetic simulation.
method: A multimodal RAG pipeline that extracts figures and contextual text from PDFs using PyMuPDF, generates unified multimodal embeddings with BLIP2 or LLaVA, stores them in a Chroma or FAISS vector database for semantic retrieval, uses OCR (Tesseract, EasyOCR) to extract dimensional annotations, applies Stable Diffusion Inpainting to clean geometric contours, and converts the result to DXF format via ezdxf for use in HFSS electromagnetic simulation. LangChain and LangGraph orchestrate the pipeline with a reflection-based verification loop to reduce hallucination.
mentioned_systems: Chroma; FAISS; BLIP2; LLaVA; Tesseract; EasyOCR; Stable Diffusion Inpainting; LangChain; LangGraph; ezdxf; HFSS; PyMuPDF; DeepErase
application_domain: Antenna design and electromagnetic simulation; extraction of geometric design information from engineering scientific literature
results_summary: The paper proposes and evaluates a Multimodal RAG (MRAG) framework that autonomously reconstructs antenna geometries from scientific PDFs into simulation-ready DXF files. The pipeline was validated on multiple antenna designs from different published papers, and HFSS simulations of the reconstructed geometries showed return loss, bandwidth, and radiation patterns closely matching the originally reported values. A performance comparison between BLIP-2 and LLaVA-1.5 demonstrated that BLIP-2 achieves higher throughput (253.3 vs. 84.9 images per minute) and lower GPU memory usage (2.52 GB vs. 4.09 GB), making it better suited for large-scale multimodal indexing and retrieval. The framework was shown to be generalizable across different antenna types and source papers, confirming its potential for scalable engineering knowledge extraction.
limitations: OCR systems (Tesseract, EasyOCR) perform poorly when image resolution is low, annotations overlap, or fonts are stylized; Minor contour deviations may occur near dense annotation regions after Stable Diffusion Inpainting; The framework is currently limited to single-layer planar antennas based on geometry; BLIP-2 has a significantly longer model load time (701.40 s) compared to LLaVA-1.5 (66.44 s)
research_gaps: Reconstructing multilayer, three-dimensional antenna configurations; Incorporating information from multiple views (side views, cross-section views, or assembly drawings); Exploring multimodal reasoning and structural inference techniques for more complex antenna structures across a variety of views

title: Product Innovation Information Using Large Language Model Based on TRIZ and Patent Mining Focusing on Sustainability
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is a TRIZ+LLM framework for product innovation; the Chroma vector database is used solely as a storage component within the RAG pipeline and is not analyzed, compared, or discussed in any depth regarding its indexing or search properties.
research_focus: Integration of TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) principles with Large Language Models to support sustainable product innovation, using publicly available patent data as a knowledge base.
method: Llama-2-7B-chat is used to summarize 3720 USPTO patents with a focus on sustainability and technical contradictions. Summarized patents are stored in a Chroma vector database. RAG technology is employed for retrieval to mitigate LLM hallucination. The TRIZ contradiction matrix is used as a problem-solving tool, and users interact via natural language queries.
application_domain: Product innovation, patent mining, and sustainability (energy efficiency)
results_summary: The paper proposes and implements an end-to-end proof-of-concept framework that combines TRIZ principles with Llama 2 and a Chroma vector database to recommend sustainable product innovations from patent data. The system was evaluated through three experiments and two use cases focused on mobile phone device sustainability. Experiments assessed the LLM's semantic understanding, context awareness, and similarity between generated abstract and claims summaries. The authors report that the system provides explainable outputs and good support for professionals seeking innovation solutions. GPU compute time and associated GHG emissions were calculated at each stage to address the environmental impact of the system itself.
limitations: Only patents from a single website (USPTO) were included in the knowledge base; The system is a proof of concept without a user-friendly front-end interface; No qualitative analysis by domain experts was conducted to assess system quality
research_gaps: Testing the system within a cloud environment; Developing a system front-end for a user-friendly interface; Incorporating and comparing more Large Language Models with extensive summarized patent samples; Extending the knowledge base to other patent repositories (Espacenet, WIPO); Conducting qualitative analysis by collating domain experts' reviews; Constructing additional use cases to test accuracy and durability; Exploring and assessing quantized LLMs in terms of relevance, accuracy, and consistency

title: Streamlining Computational Lithography With Efficient Pattern Database
relevance_reason: The paper's main subject is computational lithography and mask optimization in semiconductor manufacturing; the vector database is merely one of three components in their proposed pattern database system, used as a retrieval tool rather than being the subject of analysis, comparison, or improvement.
research_focus: Designing a pattern database for computational lithography to address challenges in inverse lithography technique (ILT), hotspot detection (HSD), and source parameter optimization in semiconductor manufacturing.
method: A three-component framework: (1) unsupervised metric learning to embed layout patterns into a vector space, (2) a vector database for high-speed pattern retrieval, and (3) a hierarchical K-neighbor graph partition method for pattern clustering and representative pattern selection.
application_domain: Computational lithography and semiconductor mask optimization (ILT, hotspot detection, source parameter optimization)
results_summary: The authors designed a pattern database combining unsupervised metric learning, a vector database for retrieval, and hierarchical K-neighbor graph partitioning for clustering. They applied the system to improve lithography hotspot detection via pattern retrieval, reporting improvements in recall and F1 score. The ILT solution-reusing strategy demonstrated reduced computational demands by leveraging past solutions for similar patterns. The hierarchical clustering method provided a systematic approach for selecting representative patterns to guide ILT and source parameter optimization. The authors report that the framework has the potential to reduce turnaround times, lower costs, and improve yields in semiconductor manufacturing.
